title: [Kernel] Add opt-in load-time MXFP4 dequantization
body:
## Summary

- model: https://huggingface.co/amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8
- add an explicit opt-in that dequantizes MXFP4 emulation weights to BF16 once during `process_weights_after_loading`;
- keep activation QDQ unchanged while avoiding repeated weight dequantization in each linear invocation;
- implement the optimization in the generic MXFP4 emulation backend so it applies to Quark, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, online quantization, and other callers.

## Motivation

On paths that select `EmulationMxfp4LinearKernel` (for example when no native MXFP4 dense kernel is available for a layer, or when `--linear-backend emulation` is requested), vLLM fake-quantizes activations each step and **dequantizes packed MXFP4 weights on every forward call**. For large models with many dense linears, repeated weight dequant dominates emulation latency and makes end-to-end serving or evaluation impractically slow.

This mirrors the MXFP8 emulation load-time dequantization introduced with [#45381](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45381) in `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel`: dequantize weights once at load, then run a plain high-precision linear with unchanged activation QDQ. Because decoded BF16 weights use roughly 2× the device memory of packed MXFP4, this feature is **opt-in and default-off** via `VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD` (unlike MXFP8 emulation, which defaults on).

## Use case

**Primary example:** Kimi K3 Quark MXFP4 dense linears on **AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950)** when the linear backend uses emulation.

```bash
VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=1 \
vllm serve amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --linear-backend emulation \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --trust-remote-code
```

The optimization is format-agnostic: any MXFP4 checkpoint routed through the emulation backend (Quark, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, online quantization, etc.) can opt in the same way. Native MXFP4 kernels, fused-MoE execution, and kernel auto-selection are unchanged when emulation is not selected.

## Enablement

Set `VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=1` to dequantize emulation weights to BF16 once at load. Default `False` preserves the existing per-call dequant path and packed-weight memory footprint. Set to `0`/`False` to opt out after enabling.

## Split from the AITER backend

The gfx950 AITER A16WFP4 backend has been removed from this PR. That integration depends on the unreleased API from [ROCm/aiter#4772](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4772) and will be handled separately only after the AITER PR is merged, released, and the AITER version is bumped in vLLM.

## Historical Kimi-K3 performance evidence

These are historical model-level integration measurements of the cached emulation fallback, recovered from this PR's earlier description. They were not rerun on the current generic, default-off implementation. Older-runtime measurements and the newer ROCm/AITER attention runtime are separate populations and must not be combined into one strict A/B series. Combined routed-A8W4 results are not an isolated speedup claim for this PR.

### Older-runtime cached fallback: concurrency sweep

| Concurrency | Cached fallback mean TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 90.97 | 10.11 |
| 4 | 109.98 | 31.59 |
| 16 | 153.79 | 68.71 |
| 32 | 273.65 | 86.36 |
| 128 | 288.38 | 88.82 |

### Older-runtime recorded emulation comparisons

| Concurrency | Full/per-call emulation TPOT (ms) | Cached emulation TPOT (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 402.43 | 90.97 |
| 4 | 177.14 | 109.98 |

No full-emulation baseline was recorded in the earlier description for C16/C32/C128; the sweep above is not a five-point paired A/B.

### Newer ROCm/AITER attention runtime

On the attention runtime associated with [ROCm/aiter#4450](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4450):

| Configuration | Concurrency | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) | Successful requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 reference | 1 | 22.995 | Not recorded in the earlier body | Not recorded in the earlier body |
| Routed A8W4 + cached shared/dense fallback | 1 | 22.551 | 33.123 | 3/3 |

The combined configuration reduced mean TPOT by 1.93% versus this BF16 reference. This is a different runtime and configuration from the older emulation comparisons, not an isolated measurement of toggling `VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD` on the current PR head.

## Historical Kimi-K3 accuracy evidence

GSM8K, 8-shot, from the historical K3 integration configuration:

| Configuration | Flexible exact match | Strict exact match |
|---|---:|---:|
| Official emulation | 96.36% | 96.36% |
| Routed A8W4 + per-call dense emulation | 96.21% | 96.21% |
| Routed A8W4 + cached dense fallback | 96.29% | 96.36% |
| Cached configuration minus official emulation | -0.07 percentage points | +0.00 percentage points |

The cached configuration stayed within the historical <=0.5 percentage-point accuracy-regression gate. These are model-level integration results, not generic unit-test guarantees or a new current-head accuracy run. They must not be attributed to the separate native A4W4 path or to the AITER A16WFP4 backend removed from this PR.

## Historical memory trade-off

| Kimi-K3 observation | Change with cached BF16 weights |
|---|---:|
| Resident dequantized-weight memory | Approximately +1.5 GiB |
| Memory available for KV cache | Approximately -3.43 GiB |

These are workload-level observations from the earlier implementation, not a universal storage multiplier. Exact memory use depends on model dimensions, dtype, allocator behavior, and the number of emulated linear layers. The current optimization remains opt-in and default-off; leave `VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=0` when preserving KV-cache capacity is more important than emulation latency.

- `27 passed`: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py`
- Ruff `v0.14.0` lint and format checks passed for all changed files
- `git diff --check` passed

title: [Kernel][DSV4.1] Fuse MXFP8 wo_b GEMM with sequence-parallel reduce-scatter
body:
## Purpose

Under sequence parallel, DeepSeek-V4.1's `wo_b` runs as an MXFP8 row-parallel GEMM followed by a TP reduce-scatter: two kernels and one HBM round trip per layer. This PR fuses them with the SM100 GEMM-RS kernel. It builds on @gau-nernst's MXFP8 support for the Kimi-K3 GEMM-RS/AR kernel (the first five commits), moves that kernel to `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/gemm_rs_ar.py` so both models share one workspace, init gate, warmup, test and benchmark, and binds V4.1's `wo_b` to it behind `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` (default off; this single flag replaces `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_RS` and gates the Kimi-K3 RS path too — `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR` is unchanged). The decoder layer skips its own `sp_reduce_scatter` when bound; RS zero-fills output rows beyond M for callers that pass an unpadded token count. Requires SM100, BF16 model dtype, sequence parallel, TP in 2..16, and FlashInfer CUTLASS or CuTe-DSL MXFP8 weights (what `linear_backend=auto` selects); anything else falls back with a warning.

No open PR fuses the V4.1 `wo_b` reduce-scatter: #57257 changes the SP all-gather side and #54151 is Kimi-K3 AG-GEMM.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py  # 2 GPUs: bf16, flashinfer_cutlass, flashinfer_cutedsl
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
    --model deepseek_v41 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl --m 128 192 256 384 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384
```

### Deploy

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 2026
```

Baseline: the same command with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0` (main's `wo_b` path).

### Benchmark

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 2026 --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 96 --num-warmups 8
```

GSM8K: lm-eval 0.4.12, `gsm8k` 5-shot chat (`--apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn`, thinking off), greedy, 1024 max tokens, all 1319 questions.

## Test Result

4xB200, TP4 + EP4 with MegaMoE (sequence parallel), FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, no speculative decoding. Kernel test: 3 passed.

Operator level (`benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py`), TP4, `wo_b` shape N=5120 with K=2048 per rank, MXFP8 CuTe-DSL layout, activation quantization included in both candidates, CUDA graphs, median over 40 samples of the slowest rank. The baseline is the model's unfused path with vLLM's own collective dispatch (custom Lamport reduce-scatter for small messages, NCCL above its size cap):

| M | vLLM linear + `sp_reduce_scatter` (us) | GEMM-RS (us) | latency |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 26.6 | 29.2 | +9.7% |
| 512 | 36.9 | 38.9 | +5.6% |
| 1024 | 48.0 | 47.1 | -2.0% |
| 2048 | 100.9 | 63.5 | -37.1% |
| 4096 | 141.8 | 96.3 | -32.1% |
| 8192 | 226.8 | 162.8 | -28.2% |
| 16384 | 428.5 | 289.2 | -32.5% |

The fused kernel wins from about 1024 tokens; below that vLLM's Lamport reduce-scatter is faster than the fused kernel's fixed flag/exit handshake. Without speculative decoding, decode batches (at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) never reach the fused path and prefill chunks are large, so serving only sees the winning region.

Torch profiler, one 8192-token prefill step on rank 0: the 40 NCCL reduce-scatter launches (9.1 ms) and 40 `wo_b` GEMMs (2.8 ms) are replaced by 40 fused launches (6.6 ms); GPU busy time per step drops from 127.1 ms to 118.1 ms (-7.1%).

Online serving, `bench serve` with fixed-length random requests, mean of two runs per arm (arms off, on, on, off with a fresh server each), zero preemptions:

| workload | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TTFT (ms) | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c16 | 1697.8 -> 1708.0 (+0.6%) | 15279.8 -> 15371.6 (+0.6%) | 1050.5 -> 1038.5 (-1.1%) | 8.40 -> 8.36 (-0.5%) |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c32 | 2592.0 -> 2668.2 (+2.9%) | 23328.4 -> 24014.2 (+2.9%) | 1565.3 -> 1512.5 (-3.4%) | 10.82 -> 10.51 (-2.9%) |
| 1024 in / 2048 out, c32 | 3178.2 -> 3324.3 (+4.6%) | 4767.4 -> 4986.5 (+4.6%) | 771.4 -> 767.5 (-0.5%) | 9.75 -> 9.27 (-5.0%) |

Run-to-run spread: baseline runs differ by 0.5% (c16), 5.4% (c32) and 16% (1k/2k); fused runs by 0.1%, 1.7% and 7%. The c16 change is within drift; c32 is at its edge with every percentile improving (p99 TTFT 4760 -> 3610 ms); the 1k/2k row is not resolved by two runs.

GSM8K, same server config:

| metric | off | on | paired changes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| flexible-extract | 95.98% (+-0.54) | 96.29% (+-0.52) | 10 became correct, 6 became wrong |
| strict-match | 79.45% (+-1.11) | 78.70% (+-1.13) | 30 became correct, 40 became wrong |

Not measured: speculative decoding (decode batches near 192 tokens would also take the fused path) and TP8. The `off` arm runs this branch with the flag unset rather than a separate main checkout; the earlier commits only touch Kimi-K3 and `cute_utils`, so V4.1's `wo_b` path is main's.

title: [CI] Emit a kernel symbol map from the csrc build (opt-in, for test selection)
body:
## Purpose

Part of the CI test-selection work in vllm-project/ci-infra (#555, #610, #611). The nightly CI runs now record which GPU kernels every step launches. To turn that into a decision ("this PR changed `csrc/foo.cu`, which steps launched a kernel from it?") CI also needs to know **which source file produced each kernel symbol**. That has to come from the real build, because the mangled names depend on template instantiations, the arch list and what CMake actually compiled.

This PR adds `tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py`, run inside the `csrc-build` Dockerfile stage right after the compile layers. Per compiled object it records the source file, the CMake target, the headers `ninja -t deps` says it read, and the kernel entry symbols `cuobjdump -symbols` finds in the fatbin. Output is one gzipped JSON, ~3.4 MB. A scratch stage `kernel-symbol-map` exposes the file and `image_build.sh` bakes that target with a local output and uploads it as a build artifact.

**Off by default.** Everything is gated on the build arg / env `VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP=1`, which only the nightly and daily full-run schedules will set. A normal build gains one `COPY` and one `RUN` that prints "Skipping", both after the compile layers so their cache is untouched. The script never fails the build; an empty map with a `reason` is the failure signal downstream.

Also regenerates `docs/assets/contributing/dockerfile-stages-dependency.png` for the new stage (pre-commit hook).

## Test Plan

Ran the image build on a fork branch with the arg set, image-build step only, three times while iterating (Buildkite `vllm/ci` builds 90006, 90008, 90011), then joined the resulting map with kernel recordings from real CI steps.

## Test Result

- Map produced in 62 s inside the (cached) `csrc-build` layer: 567 objects, 543 device objects, 10,447 kernel entry symbols, 0 `cuobjdump` errors, every object attributed to its CMake target (`_vllm_fa3_C` 194, `_C_stable_libtorch` 113, `_deepselect_C` 79, `_vllm_fa2_C` 79, `_flashmla_C` 56, ...). 89 of the 98 `.cu` files under `csrc/` appear (the rest are ROCm-only or not in the CUDA 13 arch list); 111 of 163 headers appear as dependencies.

title: [BugFix][Core] Make the structured-output grammar poll non-blocking
body:
## Purpose

Split out of #53772 at @arpera's request so it can land independently (context: #53130).

`StructuredOutputRequest._check_grammar_completion()` polled the grammar future with `result(timeout=0.0001)`, which:

- blocks 100 µs per pending future on every poll — the scheduler polls each parked structured-output request every step it traverses `skipped_waiting`, so at the backlog seen in #53130 (473 parked requests) that is ~47 ms of pure waiting per step; and
- treats any `TimeoutError` as "still compiling". Since Python 3.11 `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` *is* the builtin `TimeoutError`, so a grammar compile that **raised** `TimeoutError` (e.g. from a compile-timeout guard) was classified as pending forever instead of as a failed compile, leaving the request parked indefinitely.

The fix checks `done()` first (non-blocking) and lets `result()` surface the real exception, which is then stored as the failed-compile marker exactly as before.

**Not a duplicate**: no open PR touches this poll; the same change was previously part of #53772 and has been removed from there.


- `test_pending_grammar_future_is_not_ready` — a pending future still reports not-ready and `grammar is None`.
- `test_grammar_compile_raising_timeout_error_is_a_failure` — a future whose compile raised `TimeoutError` is reported ready with the exception as its grammar (fails on `main`, passes with this change).

## What does this PR do?

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Run the dense MLP layers on the sequence-parallel shard
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel` (the configuration that turns on `use_sequence_parallel_moe`) sporadically emits a wrong first token, stray `</think>` tokens followed by a repeated reasoning block, and occasionally byte garbage such as `ԥԥԥԥ� Canadian French, ԥԥ�1ԥ…`. DP with TP=1 and TP-only serving are clean.

`Glm5NextModel` follows the DeepSeek-V4 sequence-parallel layout: the token dimension is sharded across the TP group once at the model entry (`sp_shard`) and every layer runs its mHC and MLP on that shard, gathering only for attention. Every non-MoE module on the shard therefore has to be sequence-parallel aware. The dense MLP of the first `first_k_dense_replace` (3) layers was still constructed as a standard TP MLP, so its `down_proj` all-reduce summed the partial outputs of *different* tokens held by the two TP ranks:

- multi-token batches (prefill, concurrent decode): rows of the first three layers are mixed pairwise, hence the wrong first token / garbage under load;
- single-token decode: the peer rank holds a zero padding row, so the real token only loses half of the intermediate dimension, which is why the model still looked mostly coherent and the bug went unnoticed.

The shared experts already pass `is_sequence_parallel` (replicated weights, `disable_tp`, no collective). This PR passes the same flag to the dense `Glm5NextMLP` and adds a unit test for the layout. TP-only and DP-with-TP1 deployments do not enter this branch and are unchanged.

Related but different: #50154 describes a sequence-parallel bug in the `deepseek_v2` path (GLM-5.2), where the SP boundary sits inside the MoE block; glm5next shards the whole model, so the fix lives in the dense layer construction instead.

## Test Plan

Unit test (single process, fakes a TP=2 world in the parallel linear layers and forbids the all-reduce):

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_sequence_parallel.py -v
```

The layer-level case fails on `main` (the dense `gate_up_proj` weight is sharded to half the intermediate size) and passes with this PR.

End to end on 4x GB300, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8), FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE attention, FLASHINFER_TRTLLM FP8 MoE, `allgather_reducescatter` all2all, default CUDA graphs, prefix caching disabled, `--max-num-seqs 64`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Each chat completion is scored as anomalous if the parsed reasoning/content contains U+FFFD, non-printable characters, a run of 8+ identical non-whitespace characters, a 4-gram repetition ratio above 0.5, or more than one `</think>`. `lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot on 200 problems via `local-completions`.

## Test Result

| config | 16 prompts sequential (temp 0) | 64 prompts, concurrency 64, 1024 tok | 8 x ~15k-token prompts + 8 short, concurrent | gsm8k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP4 TP1 EP | 0 / 16 | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.935 |
| DP4 TP1 EP + MTP(3) + kv fp8 | 0 / 16 | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.94 |
| TP4 EP | 0 / 48 (3 runs) | - | - | - |
| DP2 TP2 EP, **before** | 4 / 16 | **31 / 64** | 3 / 16 | 0.95 |
| DP2 TP2 EP, **after** | 0 / 48 (3 runs) | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.935 |

Before the fix the three temperature-0 runs of the same prompt typically diverged at the first or second character (the prefill result itself was wrong). After the fix they diverge only late (character 84 to 724), the same as the TP4 EP baseline (47 to 1228), which is the usual batch-dependent nondeterminism. gsm8k is insensitive to this bug because the answers are short.

Ruled out on the way: the MNNVL Lamport custom all-gather / reduce-scatter kernels used by `sp_all_gather` / `sp_reduce_scatter` on this platform pass a 2-GPU stress test against NCCL (3000 iterations, 1 to 1024 rows x 4096 bf16, all-gather and reduce-scatter back to back, 0 mismatches).

`pre-commit` hooks `ruff-check` / `ruff-format` pass on the changed files.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Avoid NaN in the Triton softcap for large attention logits
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56578 

`apply_softcap` computed `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio becomes `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned.

This is reachable for Gemma-2 style models that set `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`: a pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. Verified on a GTX 1650 Ti with the real helper:

```text
input  : [1.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -1.0, -10000.0, 4400.0]
before : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, NaN, NaN, -0.9999, NaN, inf]
after  : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -0.9999, -50.0, 50.0]
```

The fix computes the same value as `1 - 2 / (exp(2 * S / x) + 1)`, which saturates cleanly at `+/-1` for either sign. The helper is shared by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k "50.0 and not fp8 and not q_dtype1"
```

## Test Result

- New test fails on main without the fix: `NaN` for the large scores.
- With the fix: the new test passes.
- 336 softcap tests pass. The `fp8` cases fail only on SM75, where Triton reports `fp8e4nv` is unsupported.

## Purpose

Fix garbage outputs from QuIP transforms on Blackwell GPUs under `torch.compile` + CUDA graph capture. Initially observed on RTX 5090 (SM120); since reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0. Addresses the runtime side of vllm-project/llm-compressor#2006.

## Background

The `hadacore_transform` op is declared with a mutable schema:

```cpp
ops.def("hadacore_transform(Tensor! x, bool inplace) -> Tensor");
```

Two interacting issues:

**1. Kernel ignores the `inplace` parameter (latent bug).** In `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/hadamard/hadacore/hadamard_transform_cuda.cu`, the kernel always writes to `x.data_ptr()` regardless of `inplace`:

```cpp
torch::stable::Tensor out = inplace ? x : torch::stable::empty_like(x);
hadacore::run_fht<SCALAR_TYPE>(x.data_ptr(), x.data_ptr(), x.numel(), ...);
// `inplace=False` callers receive `out`, but `out` was never written to
return torch::stable::reshape(out, res_shape);
```

The conditional copy-back cannot fire because `out` is only aliased to `x` when `inplace=True`. The path is currently unused in vLLM but is publicly exposed.

**2. Mutable schema causes inductor to elide protective clones.** In `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod.apply()`, the `.clone()` introduced in #26849 for compile robustness:

```python
x[:, start:start+length] = self.output_transform(
    x[:, start:start+length].clone(), part_id=part_id
)
```

Inductor analyzes the `Tensor!` schema, decides the clone is redundant (the op will mutate anyway), and elides it from the FX graph (verified via `TORCH_LOGS="output_code"`). The kernel ends up receiving a slice view aliasing `x`, producing garbage outputs under `torch.compile` + cudagraph. Initially observed on SM120; later also reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0 (QuIP variants: WikiText-2 PPL ~1.4e6; coherent with `enforce_eager=True`). @mgoin's `gsm8k_eval` in #28748 (0.697) used a combination that does not trigger the inductor elision: whether the bug manifests depends on the (torch version x compile/cudagraph) configuration, not the hardware.

| NVFP4A16 + QuIP, compile | RTX 5090 | ❌ Garbage | ✅ Coherent |

| `gsm8k_eval` @mgoin SpinQuant model | B200 | 0.697 (#28748) | 0.697 |

## Changes

Kernel writes to `out.data_ptr()` instead of `x.data_ptr()` (respects `inplace`); call sites in `module.py` pass `inplace=False` to opt into the non-aliasing path. The existing `.clone()` from #26849 is retained as a defensive layer.

## Reproduction

The bug manifests on any compressed-tensors checkpoint using online Hadamard transforms (QuIP) under vLLM's default `torch.compile` + cudagraph execution. The root cause is in the kernel, independent of the calibration path. It also blocks the MXFP4 W4A4 + MR-GPTQ path (where rotations contribute ~+3 pts PPL recovery vs GPTQ alone on Llama-3.1-8B) and any future recipe relying on online Hadamard rotations.

### Step 1: produce a QuIP-transformed checkpoint

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor
cd llm-compressor
pip install -e .

# QuIP + GPTQ + NVFP4A16 example from vllm-project/llm-compressor#2751 (~10 min):
gh pr checkout 2751
python examples/transform/nvfp4_quip_gptq_example.py
# produces Llama-3.1-8B-quip-gptq-nvfp4a16
```

The attached logs were produced with an equivalent minimal datafree variant (`examples/transform/quip_example.py` adapted to the NVFP4A16 scheme, on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, producing `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quip-nvfp4a16`). Both recipes trigger the same bug.

### Step 2: reproduce the failure on `main`

```bash
# vLLM main branch build (per-commit nightly wheel; the version string embeds the main commit)
pip install vllm==0.22.1rc1.dev255+g4dcd10eb0 --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python validate_nvfp4_quip.py <checkpoint_dir>
```

(`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` works around an unrelated FlashInfer sampler init failure on SM120 with this build; it does not affect the transform path.)

```python
    "The capital of France is",
    "Quantum mechanics is the branch of physics that",
    "Once upon a time, in a distant kingdom,",
    "def fibonacci(n):\n    ",
    "Translate to French: 'Hello, how are you today?'\nFrench:",
]

SAMPLING = SamplingParams(max_tokens=80, temperature=0.0)


def main() -> None:
    print(f"Loading checkpoint: {CHECKPOINT_DIR}")
    model = LLM(model=CHECKPOINT_DIR, dtype="auto")

    print(f"\nRunning {len(PROMPTS)} sanity generations...\n")
    outputs = model.generate(PROMPTS, SAMPLING)

    for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
        print(f"=== Prompt {i + 1}/{len(PROMPTS)} ===")
        print(f"PROMPT: {output.prompt!r}")
        print(f"OUTPUT: {output.outputs[0].text!r}")
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
